_**Agent (gpt-5 2025-11-11 14:53:12Z)**_

Root cause: the homepage was “frozen” and didn’t re-render when the include changed. Your site uses execute.freeze: auto at the project level, so index.qmd won’t rebuild unless Quarto detects a change in that page’s own inputs. It doesn’t track the generated include `_data/home-latest-posts.md`, so new posts didn’t show up.

What I changed
- Disabled freeze for the homepage to force re-render on each build.
  - index.qmd:1 now includes:
    - execute.freeze: false

Why this fixes it
- `_data/generate_home_sections.py` already generates `_data/home-latest-posts.md` correctly.
- With freeze disabled on the homepage, the updated include is picked up every render, so the “Latest Posts” list updates reliably.

How to verify
- Run: `quarto render index.qmd`
- Open: `_site/index.html` and scroll to “Latest Posts”
- You should see the latest three posts (e.g., “Modern Alternatives to Traditional Linux Commands”, etc.).

Notes and optional improvements
- If you prefer to keep project-level freeze, keeping only the homepage unfrozen is a good balance.
- The same “freeze vs. external data” issue can affect `news.qmd`. If you want that page to always reflect changes in `_data/news.yml`, I can also set execute.freeze: false there.
- Pre-render looks correctly configured in `_quarto.yml` to run: `python _data/generate_home_sections.py`. Make sure to commit `_data/home-latest-posts.md` so GitHub Pages picks it up.
